summary: Verified the 4 'FIXED' bugs (Task 1/1b avatar upload code, Task 2 Ask-About-Product, Task 3/5 inquiry chat messaging) and the 2 'NOT FIXED/expected-blocked' bugs (Task 4 booking, Task 6 feed) from the review request. Backend: 12/12 new pytest tests passed against the live preview API (fresh signed-up + auto-confirmed test customer, real existing provider). Frontend: full real-UI E2E pass for Task 2 (Shop -> Ask About Product -> chat opens with system message -> follow-up text sent and rendered with correct alignment). Found ONE new real bug blocking Task 5(c) (conversation not appearing in Messages/Inbox list) caused by an unrelated 405 on GET /bookings poisoning chatService.getConversations()'s error handling. Task 4 and Task 6 confirmed to fail safely (no fake success, no crash) as expected.

critical.issue: No local route exists for GET /bookings (only POST /bookings is defined in server.py). Calling GET returns 405 Method Not Allowed. This is called by chatService.getConversations() BEFORE it fetches the (now-fixed) GET /conversations endpoint, and an uncaught 405 here trips the outer try/catch in getConversations(), wiping out the entire conversation list -- so a correctly-created inquiry/consultation conversation never appears in the Messages/Inbox screen (chat/list.tsx shows 'No conversations yet' even though the conversation and its messages exist and are fetchable directly). This directly breaks TASK 5(c) which was explicitly asked to be verified.

minor.issue: All return 404 locally (no local implementation, purely Railway-proxied like the other blocked items). This means: (1) Home screen 'Featured Providers' always shows 'No providers available right now', (2) navigating to any /provider/{id} profile page (needed to reach the 'Ask a Question' button for Task 3, and to reach the 'Book Now' flow for Task 4) fails to load at all. Not one of the 6 bugs in scope, but it materially blocked full E2E UI verification of Task 3 and Task 4 -- had to fall back to direct API verification for those.

This endpoint was NOT included in the metadata-column fix applied to POST /conversations/{id}/messages -- _chat_row() at line ~2647 still builds the DB insert payload with top-level is_masked/original_content/location_data/invoice_data keys, which don't exist as columns on the real `chats` table schema per the same comment block just above it. It would still fail with the same root-cause bug described in Task 2/3 if ever called. Currently dead code (grep confirms the frontend never calls '/chat/messages'), so no live user impact today, but flagging so it isn't missed if this endpoint gets wired up later.

integration_issues.issue: Inquiry conversation created via 'Ask About Product' does not appear in /chat/list (Messages) even though GET /conversations/{id}/messages confirms the messages exist. Root cause: chatService.getConversations() throws on GET /bookings?auth_id=... (405, see backend_issues.critical) before it ever processes the /conversations response.

issues: Zero testID attributes found anywhere under /app/frontend/app (grep -rl testID returned 0 files). login.tsx, signup.tsx, chat/[counterpartAuthId].tsx, provider/[id].tsx, shop/[id].tsx all rely on visible text/placeholder for interaction, which is fragile for automated regression testing going forward.

react_native_issues.issue: Could not fully exercise the avatar upload flow end-to-end in the Expo web preview via Playwright: Alert.alert() with multiple action buttons ('Cancel'/'Take Photo'/'Choose from Gallery') does not render any visible dialog on web (known RN-web Alert limitation, not a code bug). This blocked automated verification of the actual image-picker -> upload -> Alert('Success') -> instant UI refresh chain. Static code review confirms the described fix (removal of the broken PUT /api/users/{id} call) is correctly applied in both files -- recommend a manual/device (Expo Go) smoke test or main-agent self-test for full confidence on this specific item.

action_items: HIGH: Fix chatService.getConversations() in src/services/chat.service.ts so a failure fetching /bookings (405, no local GET route) does not also discard the successfully-fetched /conversations (inquiry/consultation) data -- wrap the /bookings fetch in its own try/catch (similar to how the /conversations fetch already has one) instead of relying on one shared outer try/catch for both.
Consider adding a local GET /bookings list endpoint (or explicitly catching/handling its absence) since it's relied upon by both the Bookings tab and the Messages inbox.

Confirmed working, no action needed: Task 2 (Ask About Product), Task 3/5 backend chat fix (create_inquiry, send/get conversation messages, mark-read, unread-count), Task 4 (bookings fails safely), Task 6 (feed fails safely).
Optional/low priority: apply the same metadata-column fix to the unused POST /chat/messages (_chat_row) code path for future-proofing, or remove it if genuinely dead code.
Optional: add testID attributes across auth and chat screens to make future regression testing more reliable.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py conversations/chat fix (lines ~2340-2750) is well-structured: clear comments explaining the real DB schema mismatch, a small set of shared helper functions (_chat_metadata_payload, _normalize_chat_row, _to_db_message_type) reused across create_inquiry/send_conversation_message/get_conversation_messages, consistent with the 'no schema change' constraint.
_chat_row() (used only by the currently-unreferenced POST /chat/messages) was missed by the metadata-column fix and would still be broken if ever wired up -- worth a follow-up cleanup pass.

chatService.getConversations() (chat.service.ts) mixes two independent data sources (booking-chats via /bookings, and shared conversations via /conversations) inside a single try block, so a failure in the first silently hides success in the second -- this is the root cause of the Messages/Inbox regression found in this session.

rca_of_issue: Task 5(c) bug: chat.service.ts getConversations() does `const bookings = await apiService.get('/bookings?auth_id=...')` as the FIRST statement inside its only try block. Locally only POST /bookings is registered in server.py (line 253) -- there is no GET /bookings route -- so FastAPI returns 405 for the GET. This throws inside getConversations(), is caught by the single outer catch block, logged as '[chat] failed to load conversations', and the function returns [] immediately -- it never reaches the later `apiService.get('/conversations')` call (which itself is separately wrapped in its own .catch(() => []) and would have succeeded, since that's the endpoint fixed this session). Net effect: the newly-fixed and correctly-working /conversations data never reaches the Messages/Inbox screen because of this unrelated method-not-allowed error earlier in the same function.
